flashcard_questions.q: What does place mean in the marketing mix?
flashcard_questions.a: How a business gets its product or service to the customer.
The route a product takes from the manufacturer to the final consumer.
The manufacturer sells straight to the consumer with no intermediary involved.
A business selling goods to consumers through a physical bricks-and-mortar shop.
A business buying in very large quantities from manufacturers and selling on to retailers.
A business that sells goods to consumers over the internet.
A shop that is not part of a chain, usually started by its owner.

flashcard_questions.q: Which term describes a business with both physical stores and an online shop?
What is the profit advantage of direct selling for a manufacturer?
flashcard_questions.a: It keeps all the profit, because no middleman takes a cut.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the cost drawback of direct selling?
flashcard_questions.a: Distribution costs per sale are higher than delivering in bulk.

flashcard_questions.q: What distribution saving does selling through a wholesaler give a manufacturer?
flashcard_questions.a: It ships to one wholesaler instead of many retailers.

flashcard_questions.q: Why are profit margins squeezed most in the wholesaling channel?
flashcard_questions.a: Two intermediaries each take a share.

flashcard_questions.q: Why can an e-tailer undercut a high street shop on price?
flashcard_questions.a: Its fixed costs are lower because it pays no rent on shops.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the main trust problem for an e-tailer?
flashcard_questions.a: There is no face-to-face interaction with the customer.

flashcard_questions.q: What cost problem do free returns create for SportShoes.com?

notes: 15 cards: 8 term→definition (place, distribution channel, direct selling, retailer, wholesaler, e-tailer, independent retailer, clicks and mortar), 6 single-fact advantage/disadvantage cards, one for each channel or selling method, and 1 case-study fact (SportShoes.com free returns).
